startup_cache.definition: Fresh owned worker container-image cache versus that worker after first startup; dependencies remain warm; Wasm component/provider caches are new on both starts.

policy: Keep every scheduled attempt, failure, partial run and recovery; never replace a bad result with a passing run.
Alternate Java-first and Wasm-first pairs/sweeps. Run only one implementation under load at a time.
Historical evidence is retained with hashes and explicit provenance; do not pool different protocols or count derived summaries twice.
Freeze source hashes, live application imageIDs, templates, application and secret/config hashes before any measurement. Changes require a new campaign.

Footprint baseline gate: 180-second warmup with zero failed/dropped requests, followed by a separate 30-second 100/s gate with p95 <500ms. Two failed baseline gates in a suite halt that suite; never silently restart the host.

Footprint requires no pod identity/restart/readiness changes and >=80% complete per-container telemetry coverage. Idle uses seconds 60-90; load uses seconds 150-210. CPU uses a 60-second rate wholly within each phase.

Density removes application CPU limits and requires all-node CPU coverage and sampled utilization <60%. An unready or replaced pod is inconclusive_runtime unless separate evidence proves memory exhaustion. Density slots are projections, not concurrent replica tests.
Startup uses the existing guarded fresh-worker driver. Exclude both cold and cached members if either member of a pair is invalid; retain both originals. No automatic replacement pairs.
Require mains and an open lid. An interruption is classified as environmental, not application capacity. Bound every load and startup; preserve recovery checkpoints.
Report median and observed range across independent runs, sample sizes, all failures and exclusions. These local application deployments do not establish a universal language/runtime ranking.
